hypothesis: Detection models trained on the Chapter 6/7 baselines can be made significantly more robust to realistic distribution shifts and unseen watermark-removal attacks by (a) training with explicit distribution-shift-aware regimes (domain adaptation and attack hold-out), and (b) adding calibrated uncertainty-based abstention, without materially degrading risk-weighted performance on in-distribution data.

baseline.description: Current best-performing image (Chapter 6) and video (Chapter 7) watermark-removal detectors trained only on the canonical training distribution, evaluated with a single fixed decision threshold tuned on an in-distribution validation split, without explicit domain adaptation, robustness regularization, or abstention.

models.name: img_cnn_vanilla
models.notes: Trained on standard training set with cross-entropy loss, no explicit robustness techniques beyond default regularization.

models.name: vid_3dcnn_vanilla
models.notes: Frame-windowed 3D CNN, uniform sampling, trained with cross-entropy.

evaluation_protocol.thresholding: Single fixed threshold per model chosen to maximize F1 on in-distribution validation set (no risk-weighting).
domains: Out-of-distribution sets not seen during training: Wild-Image-OOD, Wild-Video-OOD, HeldOut-Attack-Families
attacks_included_for_testing: Geometric transforms (resize, crop, rotation) seen during training
JPEG compression levels seen during training
A subset of diffusion/inpainting-based removal attacks used in Chapter 8

treatment.description: Apply domain adaptation / robustness strategies and calibrated uncertainty-based abstention while keeping core architectures unchanged.

variants.name: img_cnn_da_erm
variants.type: CNN image classifier with domain-adversarial adaptation and attack-family hold-out training
changes_vs_baseline: Introduce domain-adversarial training using gradient reversal on features to align Lab vs. Wild distributions where unlabeled Wild-Image-Train-U data is available.
Hold out at least one attack family (e.g., diffusion-based resynthesis) entirely from training for robustness evaluation (used only in HeldOut-Attack-Families test set).

variants.name: img_cnn_da_erm_ua
variants.type: img_cnn_da_erm plus uncertainty-aware abstention and calibration
changes_vs_baseline: Use Monte Carlo dropout or deep ensembles to estimate predictive uncertainty.
Apply temperature scaling on a held-out calibration set (Lab-Image-Cal and Wild-Image-Cal) to improve probability calibration.
Introduce an abstention region defined by a maximum acceptable predictive entropy or minimum confidence, tuned under a risk-weighted objective.

variants.name: vid_3dcnn_da_erm
variants.type: 3D CNN video classifier with domain-adversarial adaptation and temporal augmentation
changes_vs_baseline: Domain-adversarial feature alignment for Lab-Video-Train vs. unlabeled Wild-Video-Train-U.
Hold-out of at least one complex video attack (e.g., segment-wise diffusion editing) for robustness evaluation only.
Additional temporal jitter and sampling-stride augmentation.

variants.name: vid_3dcnn_da_erm_ua
variants.type: vid_3dcnn_da_erm plus uncertainty-aware abstention and calibration
changes_vs_baseline: Use temporal ensembles or MC dropout over time windows for uncertainty estimation.
Apply temperature scaling and scenario-specific threshold tuning for video.
Add abstention on high-uncertainty clips, aggregating abstention decisions at the asset level.

comparison_plan: Compare img_cnn_vanilla vs img_cnn_da_erm on in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance without abstention.
Compare img_cnn_da_erm vs img_cnn_da_erm_ua to quantify benefits and costs of abstention and calibration.
Analogous comparisons for video: vid_3dcnn_vanilla vs vid_3dcnn_da_erm vs vid_3dcnn_da_erm_ua.
Evaluate all models on HeldOut-Attack-Families and Wild-* OOD sets with identical workloads and metrics.

workloads.name: W1-in-distribution-lab-image
workloads.description: Evaluate all image models on the held-out lab validation and test sets that match the training distribution.
workloads.attack_profile: Only transformation/attack families already seen during training: standard JPEG compression, modest crops/resizes, light denoising.
workloads.usage: Baseline reference to quantify robustness cost on in-distribution performance for each treatment variant.

workloads.name: W2-in-distribution-lab-video
workloads.description: Evaluate all video models on the held-out lab validation and test sets matching the training distribution.
workloads.attack_profile: Frame-wise or segment-wise removal operations identical to those used for training (no unseen attacks).
workloads.usage: Measure any regression in standard lab performance due to domain adaptation or abstention.

workloads.name: W3-ood-wild-image-benign-shift
workloads.description: Test image models on in-the-wild images without explicit new removal attacks but with natural distribution shift (different capture devices, content domains, resolutions).
workloads.attack_profile: No synthetic removal beyond what occurs naturally; focus on covariate shift (content type, noise, compression pipelines).
workloads.usage: Assess robustness to benign domain shift independent of adversarial removal innovations.

workloads.name: W4-ood-wild-video-benign-shift
workloads.description: Test video models on in-the-wild videos with natural distribution shift (platform-specific transcoding, variable frame rates, user edits).
workloads.attack_profile: Primarily non-adversarial transformations from user workflows and platform pipelines.
workloads.usage: Evaluate temporal robustness and calibration under realistic platform-type variation.

workloads.name: W5-heldout-attack-families-image
workloads.description: Stress-test image models on synthetic datasets built with attack families that were explicitly held out of training (e.g., novel diffusion/inpainting schemes, extreme recompression, combined geometric+frequency attacks).
workloads.attack_profile: Only attacks belonging to HeldOut-Attack-Families defined in Chapter 8 (e.g., diffusion_resynthesis_v2, adversarial_inpainting_v2) and not used in training or validation.
workloads.usage: Measure generalization to unseen adversarial strategies and quantify benefits of domain adaptation and abstention.

workloads.name: W6-heldout-attack-families-video
workloads.description: Stress-test video models on held-out adversarial attack families targeting watermark removal in video streams.
workloads.attack_profile: Segment-wise diffusion editing, cross-frame inpainting, and codec-level artifacts not seen during training.
workloads.usage: Quantify robustness under sophisticated video-specific unseen removal strategies.

workloads.name: W7-scenario-based-threshold-eval
workloads.description: Evaluate all models under multiple operational scenarios with different cost structures and prevalence assumptions using a shared log of scores and uncertainties.
workloads.data_source: Combined evaluation logs from W1–W6 (scores, uncertainties, metadata).
workloads.attack_profile: Inherited from contributing source datasets (lab, benign OOD, held-out attacks).
workloads.usage: Compute scenario-specific thresholds, abstention policies, and calibration diagnostics without retraining models; used for 9.5 (Calibration, threshold selection, and scenario-based tuning).

workloads.name: W8-continuous-eval-simulation
workloads.description: Simulate a production-like monitoring loop by streaming mixed Lab and Wild content with time-varying distributions, logging metrics for ongoing evaluation.
workloads.data_source: Synthetic time-sliced streams constructed from Lab-* and Wild-* datasets, stored as event sequences.
labels: Time-slice and cohort metadata (e.g., platform, region, content category)
workloads.attack_profile: Mix of benign shift and held-out attacks at varying rates over time (e.g., attack prevalence spikes beginning at time slice t>=T0).
workloads.usage: Exercise monitoring dashboards and drift detection logic; evaluate whether robustness and abstention policies maintain acceptable risk levels as distributions evolve.

data_splits: Use fixed dataset versions and splits: no changes to train/val/test partitions once defined.
Ensure that HeldOut-Attack-Families data is never included in any training or calibration set for any model.
Use identical evaluation subsets for all model variants per workload.
randomness: Set and log global seeds for Python, NumPy, and framework (PyTorch or TensorFlow) for every run.
If using GPU, enable deterministic operations where supported and log any operations that are non-deterministic.
preprocessing: Use identical input preprocessing pipelines (resize, normalization, color space) for all model variants, implemented as shared modules under `src/preprocessing/`.
Disable any online data augmentation at evaluation; augmentation allowed only at training time, with configurations logged.
thresholding_and_calibration: For baseline models, choose thresholds solely on in-distribution Lab-*-Val data.
For treatment models with calibration, use dedicated calibration splits (Lab-* and Wild-* calibration datasets) and apply the same calibration protocol and search grid.
Do not re-tune thresholds separately per test workload except in W7, where scenario-based tuning is explicitly studied and logged.
hardware_and_runtime: Run baseline and treatment model evaluations on the same hardware class (e.g., same GPU type or CPU-only setup).
Limit batch sizes to avoid OOM; keep evaluation batch sizes constant across models for fair latency comparisons.
governance_and_logging: Log model version, config hash, git commit hash, dataset manifest, and environment hash for each run.
Ensure no cross-contamination of labeled Wild data into unsupervised target-only splits if the scenario assumes unlabeled target domains.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.description: Overall fraction of correctly classified samples (or assets) across all classes.

metrics.name: precision_watermark_removed
metrics.description: Positive predictive value when predicting 'watermark_removed'.

metrics.name: recall_watermark_removed
metrics.description: True positive rate for 'watermark_removed' cases.

metrics.name: f1_watermark_removed
metrics.description: Harmonic mean of precision and recall for 'watermark_removed'.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate_watermark_removed
metrics.description: False positive rate when predicting 'watermark_removed' vs. all non-removed cases.

metrics.name: false_negative_rate_watermark_removed
metrics.description: False negative rate on 'watermark_removed' cases.

metrics.name: auroc_watermark_removed
metrics.description: Area under the ROC curve for binary discrimination of 'watermark_removed' vs. others using raw scores.

metrics.name: auprc_watermark_removed
metrics.description: Area under the precision-recall curve for the 'watermark_removed' class.

metrics.name: ece
metrics.description: Expected Calibration Error over probability bins for the predicted class probabilities.

metrics.name: max_calibration_error
metrics.description: Maximum absolute difference between predicted confidence and empirical accuracy across bins.

metrics.name: brier_score
metrics.description: Mean squared error between predicted probability for 'watermark_removed' and actual label (0/1).

metrics.name: abstention_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of inputs for which the model abstains from making a hard classification.

metrics.name: conditional_f1_watermark_removed_nonabstained
metrics.description: F1 score on 'watermark_removed' restricted to non-abstained samples.

metrics.name: risk_weighted_cost
metrics.description: Expected cost per sample using scenario-specific misclassification and abstention costs (e.g., C_FP, C_FN, C_ABSTAIN).

metrics.name: latency_p50
metrics.description: Median end-to-end model inference latency per sample (image or video clip).

metrics.name: latency_p95
metrics.description: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency.

metrics.name: throughput
metrics.description: Effective processing rate under the evaluation workload.

metrics.name: drift_score_input
metrics.description: Statistical drift score between current input distribution and training distribution (e.g., KL divergence or population stability index on selected features).

metrics.name: drift_score_output
metrics.description: Drift of model output score distribution (e.g., KL divergence between score histograms over time windows).

metrics.name: evasion_rate_heldout_attacks
metrics.description: Proportion of watermark-removed samples under HeldOut-Attack-Families that are incorrectly classified as non-removed and not abstained.

primary: On held-out attack workloads (W5 and W6), treatment models with domain adaptation and abstention (img_cnn_da_erm_ua, vid_3dcnn_da_erm_ua) reduce evasion_rate_heldout_attacks by at least 25% relative (i.e., (baseline_evasion - treatment_evasion) / baseline_evasion >= 0.25) while keeping conditional_f1_watermark_removed_nonabstained on in-distribution workloads (W1 and W2) within 2 percentage points absolute of the baseline models.

For benign OOD workloads (W3 and W4), treatment models achieve lower risk_weighted_cost than baselines under at least two operational scenarios defined in W7 (e.g., 'high-sensitivity compliance review' and 'low-latency user-facing flagging') after scenario-based threshold tuning.
secondary: Treatment models achieve a reduction in ece of at least 30% relative on W3–W6 without degrading auroc_watermark_removed by more than 2 percentage points absolute.

Under continuous evaluation simulation (W8), drift_score_input and drift_score_output correlate with degradations in recall_watermark_removed such that an alerting rule based on these drift metrics would have flagged performance drops before a 10 percentage point absolute loss in recall on any time segment.
Abstention_rate on W5–W6 remains below 40% while still meeting the primary criteria on evasion_rate_heldout_attacks.
governance_alignment: Robustness reporting templates (see evidence_schema) must expose at least: domain, attack profile, main performance metrics, abstention behavior, and calibration diagnostics, in a form suitable for compliance review.
All configuration and environment details needed for auditors to reproduce W1–W6 results are captured in the experiment logs and artifacts.

failure_modes.name: robustness_gain_with_excessive_abstention
failure_modes.description: Treatment models achieve lower evasion_rate_heldout_attacks primarily by abstaining on a large majority of OOD or attacked samples, resulting in unacceptably high abstention_rate and degraded operational utility.
indicators: conditional_f1_watermark_removed_nonabstained remains similar to or worse than baselines, despite lower evasion_rate_heldout_attacks

failure_modes.name: in_distribution_performance_collapse
failure_modes.description: Domain adaptation or calibration significantly harms performance on lab in-distribution data, undermining reliability under well-understood conditions.
indicators: Drop in f1_watermark_removed on W1 or W2 greater than 3 percentage points absolute vs baseline.
Significant increase in false_positive_rate_watermark_removed or false_negative_rate_watermark_removed on W1 or W2 beyond governance thresholds defined in Chapter 3 and 12.

failure_modes.name: miscalibrated_under_shift
failure_modes.description: Treatment models appear well calibrated on lab calibration sets but remain poorly calibrated on Wild and HeldOut-Attack workloads, leading to overconfident wrong decisions.
indicators: ece on W3–W6 remains within 10% of or worse than baseline ece despite calibration.
max_calibration_error concentrated in high-confidence bins that contain many errors.

failure_modes.name: drift_detection_not_predictive
failure_modes.description: Drift metrics fail to predict or correlate with drops in key performance metrics under W8 continuous-eval simulation.
indicators: Segmentation of W8 streams into time windows shows large swings (>10 percentage points) in recall_watermark_removed without concurrent significant change in drift_score_input or drift_score_output.
Alert rules based on drift would either trigger constantly (false alarms) or miss major degradations.

failure_modes.name: unfair_robustness_degradation_across_cohorts
failure_modes.description: Robustness improvements or degradations are not uniform across cohorts (e.g., content categories, geographies), potentially raising fairness or regulatory issues.
indicators: Subgroup analyses in evidence_schema reveal >10 percentage point gaps in f1_watermark_removed or evasion_rate_heldout_attacks between cohorts before vs. after applying treatments.
Abstention disproportionately concentrated in certain cohorts.

failure_modes.name: non_reproducible_results
failure_modes.description: Substantial variance in key metrics under repeated runs with fixed seeds and dataset splits, undermining trust in reported robustness gains.
indicators: Repeated training of the same treatment model under identical configs (n>=3) yields standard deviation of auroc_watermark_removed > 0.02 on the same workload.
Config or environment drift detected via mismatched hashes or dependency versions in logs.

recommended: 1–2 NVIDIA GPUs with at least 16 GB memory (e.g., V100, T4, A10) for training and evaluation of both image and video models.
At least 1 TB of available disk storage for datasets and checkpoints (image + video + logs).
minimum: Single GPU with 8 GB memory for image-only experiments; video workloads may need to be downscaled or sub-sampled.
500 GB disk if video datasets are pruned or compressed.

os: Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+), or equivalent POSIX environment. Docker images provided for reproducibility.
languages_and_frameworks: PyTorch >= 2.0 or TensorFlow >= 2.11 (book repository defaults to one; use that default).
NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, OpenCV, Pandas, Matplotlib/Seaborn or Plotly for plotting.
environment_management: Conda or venv environment using `environment.yml` or `requirements.txt` from the repository root.
Optional: Docker with Docker Compose using provided `docker/` configuration.

prerequisites: Create and activate environment: `conda env create -f environment.yml && conda activate ai-watermark-det` or equivalent using `requirements.txt`.
Download or generate datasets according to Chapter 4 and 8 instructions; ensure paths under `datasets/` match those referenced in this spec.

Confirm that baseline models from Chapters 6 and 7 have been trained and checkpoints stored under `experiments/ch6_image_models/checkpoints/` and `experiments/ch7_video_models/checkpoints/` as per their READMEs.

steps.title: Prepare robustness-specific data splits
notes: This script should construct the unlabeled target sets, calibration splits, Wild-*-Benign sets, and HeldOut-Attack-Families datasets described in the workloads.
Verify the generated `datasets/ch9_robustness/manifest.json` to ensure dataset statistics make sense (class balance, attack counts).

steps.title: Train domain-adapted image and video models
notes: Configs should reference the same base architecture as the baseline models and add domain-adversarial objectives and attack hold-out rules.
Training logs and checkpoints should be saved under `experiments/ch9_robustness/runs/` with clear run IDs.

steps.title: Train or fit calibration and uncertainty components
notes: These scripts should perform temperature scaling and configure uncertainty metrics (e.g., MC dropout passes, ensemble size).
Resulting calibration parameters must be stored in model-specific subdirectories referenced in evaluation configs.

steps.title: Run standardized evaluations across workloads W1–W6
notes: The evaluation script must load both baseline and treatment checkpoints and compute all metrics defined in this spec.
Raw predictions, probabilities, and uncertainties should be logged to `experiments/ch9_robustness/logs/{model}/{workload}/predictions.parquet` or equivalent.

steps.title: Run scenario-based threshold tuning (W7)
notes: Define scenario configs (e.g., `high_sensitivity.yaml`, `balanced.yaml`, `low_latency.yaml`) specifying class prevalence and cost matrices.
The script should output scenario-optimized thresholds, abstention policies, and associated risk_weighted_cost for each model and workload.

steps.title: Simulate continuous evaluation and monitoring (W8)
notes: The monitoring script should compute metrics over sliding windows (e.g., hourly or per N samples), compute drift_score_input and drift_score_output, and log alerts according to pre-defined rules.
Outputs should include time series plots and summary statistics suitable for inclusion in robustness reports.

steps.title: Generate robustness experiment reports
notes: Reports should follow the evidence_schema structure below, generating JSON and optionally PDF/HTML summaries.
At minimum, generate a 'per-domain/per-attack' report and a 'time-series monitoring' report.

reproducibility_checks: Re-run at least one evaluation workload (e.g., W5-heldout-attack-families-image) for one treatment model with the same config; verify that results match within a narrow tolerance.
Archive `config.yaml`, git commit hashes, and environment file snapshots alongside each major report.

workload_results.attack_profile: string (human-readable description or ID linking to Chapter 8 attack configs)

metrics.risk_weighted_cost: float or null if not evaluated
metrics.evasion_rate_heldout_attacks: float or null (only for heldout attack workloads)

metrics_by_model.notes: string (optional commentary, e.g., observed anomalies or training deviations)

prevalence_assumptions.p_other_classes: mapping from class to float or null

time_window_spec.window_size: integer (e.g., number of samples per window or seconds)

governance_notes.risk_assessment: string (narrative summary of robustness risks identified, including key failure modes observed).
governance_notes.operational_recommendations: string (recommendations for threshold settings, abstention policies, monitoring alerts).
governance_notes.limitations_and_caveats: string (known limitations, data gaps, generalization concerns).
governance_notes.compliance_alignment: string (mapping of experiment outcomes to relevant regulatory or internal policy requirements).
